6309506810853509365:
Li Zhenzhen doesn't hate those who come after her.
After all, she has taken the lives of their loved ones to settle a debt, and so they have every right to seek revenge.
In this world, everything was settled with a balance of blood. Some debts were repaid with kindness, others with vengeance.
Life and death were always a transaction.
Her only regret is that the moment of death comes too soon.
She couldn't pack her things and leave for the South with that man.

Throughout her life, she has had many roles.
She is the elusive swordswoman, the Lunar Goddess; she is the villain who slaughtered warriors; she is the keeper of secrets, the one forever in debt.
But when it comes to the end of it all, she doesn't want to be any of these things.
She simply wants to be herself.
The untainted Li Zhenzhen.
Much like the flowers she planted.

The Moonflower, born from the mud, unnoticed by the world, yet still bowing to the moon and sleeping with the wind.
If there is a next life, she hopes to be nothing more than a flower.

6302461392367714574: Three Steps of Yangguan (also known as Yangguan Tune or Weicheng Tune) is a traditional Chinese piece, adapted from A Farewell Song to Yuan'er by Wang Wei: "No dust is raised on the road wet with morning rain. The willows by the hotel look so fresh and green. I invite you to drink a cup of wine again. The Yangguan Pass, no more friends will be seen." During the Tang Dynasty, this piece was arranged as a Guqin song, consisting of three main sections. In addition to repeatedly singing the original verses, several new lines were added, expanding on the imagery of the poem. The line "The Yangguan Pass, no more friends will be seen" is sung three times, which led to the name Three Steps of Yangguan.
